name: Gothic Night
summary: Moonlit cursed churchyard in detailed pixel art: a banded light map darkens a cold world; only faces, lanterns and candles glow warm.
description: A cold, desaturated night in detailed 1:1 pixel art: mossy gravestones, dead trees, cobble paths and leaf litter under drifting mist. Everything is painted fully lit in muted blue-grey, purple and moss ramps, then a per-frame banded light map (moonlight ambient + vignette + warm point lights) is multiplied over it. The only warm colours are the hero's flickering carved face, lanterns, seeds and candles, and enemies keep tiny emissive eyes that pierce the dark.

difficulty.why: Detailed pixel sprites, and every new object has to fit into the lighting system – dark yet still readable is a balancing act.

technique.resolution: 1 art pixel = 1 world unit: the 360-unit-tall view is a 360-row buffer, integer upscale up = max(1, round(screenH / 360)), nearest neighbour. Sprites are baked once into small canvases; ground chunks of 256 × 256 px are generated per pixel in time slices.
technique.summary: Sprites are painted per pixel from shaded shapes (sphere normals lit by one moon direction), quantised into hand-made ramps with Bayer-8 dither and wrapped in a #0b0910 outline. A light map canvas (ambient #687cb2 with banded vignette, drifting cloud light, banded point-light sprites) is multiplied onto the ground at 100 % and onto entities at 55 %, then bloom is added with 'lighter' and emissive pixels are drawn unlit on top.
technique.linework: 1-px near-black outline #0b0910 around every sprite (4-neighbour), added by a pass after painting; ghosts use a cool #141a2e outline, gems #061c24, seeds #2a1606, crit digits #2a0606. No outlines on ground textures; ground forms are separated by dark mortar/gap pixels and cast shadows.
technique.shading: Ramp quantisation: tone = 0.45 + shade(normal) * 0.42, picked from 3–7 step ramps with Bayer-8 dither (strength 0.3–0.5). Light comes from the upper left (normalised -0.52, -0.64, 0.56); tone canvases add +0.17 on left edges, +0.1 top, −0.15 right, −0.08 bottom. Colour transitions (purple top into cream body) are dithered.
technique.lighting: Per-frame light map: ambient moonlight rgb(104,124,178), 5-band dithered vignette down to 50 %, drifting dark cloud texture added, then point lights as banded radial sprites (hero 96 × 78 warm, lanterns 42 × 34, candles 34 × 26, red grave lights 20 × 15, cyan gems, pale ghost glows, green brute cores). Lights flicker with noise (0.86 ± 0.14). Multiplied onto ground (alpha 1) and entities (alpha 0.55).
technique.texture: Ground is per-pixel procedural: dithered soil, grass tufts revealed by per-pixel thresholds against a coverage field (dark rim where they end), sorted leaf litter with drop shadows, Worley cobbles and flagstone slabs with lit top-left edges, 3/4-view cast shadows from the row above. Decals: skulls, bones, candle stubs, puddles, grave mounds, roots, cracks, dead flowers.

paletteRules: Author every colour fully lit; the light map turns it into night. Never pre-darken sprites.
Cold, desaturated ramps (blue-grey, violet, moss, plum) for 90% of the image; warm orange/yellow only on light sources and emissive details.
Emissive colours (carved face, eyes, flames, embers, gems, souls, numbers) are drawn after the light pass and are the brightest pixels on screen.
Each material gets its own 3–7 step ramp; tones are picked with Bayer-8 dither, never blended.
Enemy families are identified by eye colour: toxic green turnips, cyan ghosts, green-cored brutes.
Outlines are always near-black #0b0910, never pure black and never coloured (except cool ghost/gem outlines).

background.summary: A moonlit moor and churchyard generated per pixel: biome fields (grass, moss, leaf litter, cobble paths, flagstone plazas, graveyard density) are sampled on an 8-px grid and interpolated; each layer reveals its own tileable 256² texture where a per-pixel threshold falls below the field value, so edges break into single tufts, stones and leaves.
layers: Soil: dithered 6-step ramp from two fbm octaves, pebbles of 2–3 px cobble tones
Grass / moss: per-tuft threshold (Worley clumps + fbm) against the grass coverage field; pixels within 0.035 of the threshold are darkened × 0.72 for a rim
Dead leaves: 2900 tiny 4–6-px leaf shapes per tile in 4 families, sorted by threshold, each casting a 1-px offset shadow (× 0.72)
Flagstones (plazas) and cobbles (paths): slabs/Worley stones with a lit top-left edge and dark gaps, per-stone thresholds; 3/4-view cast shadow × 0.62 on the row below
Global brightness 0.9–1.1 and slight hue drift from low-frequency fbm

Decals baked into the chunk: grave mounds, open graves, roots around trees, puddles with moon reflection, floor slabs, cracks, moss patches, skulls and bones, candle stubs, dead flowers, twigs, single leaves
Per frame: two drifting banded mist layers (alpha ≤ 0.2 and 0.12), then the light map multiply

characters.summary: The hero is a 22 × 34 px painted sprite (24 × 36 with outline): a 15 × 13 ribbed pumpkin head lit from the upper left with a 28-pixel carved face, a wine scarf whose tail flutters through 4 positions, a violet trapezoid cloak with a lit left edge, two dark folds and a ragged hem, dark trousers and boots. 4 walk frames (legs ±2 px, 1-px lift, cloak sway) and 2 idle frames (bob ±1). The carved face is a separate emissive overlay that flickers between 3 brightness levels.
rules: Paint shapes per pixel: ellipse + sphere-normal shading + ramp pick with Bayer dither, then a 1-px #0b0910 outline
Big readable head (about 40% of the height) carrying the character's colour identity
Faces and eyes are emissive pixel lists drawn after the light so they read in the dark
4-frame walks, 2-frame idles, mirrored canvases for facing
Feet anchor at the outline's bottom row; hero shadow is an 8 × 2.5 dithered ellipse
Every actor that should be found in the dark gets a light sprite or a glow (ghost pale blue, brute green core)

effects.name: Flickering carved face
effects.how: Face pixels redrawn after the light from a 4-step ramp; flick(t) = 0.86 + 0.09 * noise + 0.05 * sin(23t) selects level 2 (> 0.95), 1 (> 0.84) or 0. The same flicker scales the 96 × 78 hero light.

effects.name: Ember trail
effects.how: Single 1-px particles rising from the pumpkin every 0.16 s, wobbling ±1 px, colour stepping down the fire ramp #fff2b8 → #7a1c06 with life; drawn emissive.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: 9 × 9 cream seed baked in 16 rotations with #2a1606 outline, 4-pixel trail #ffc848 #ff8a1c #c8460c #7a1c06 at 3 + 2.2j px behind, a 14 × 11 warm light and a small additive bloom.

effects.name: Hit / kill
effects.how: Turnips spray juice pixels (#3a0a26…#bc3068) and white/yellow sparks; ghosts burst into frost sparks and mist; death flashes the sprite white for 0.18 s, half-alpha to 0.4 s, plus a white 15 × 13 light; a teal soul (7 × 12, dithered tail) rises with its own light.

effects.name: Spawn
effects.how: Ground enemies rise out of the soil (sprite revealed bottom-up with outQuad) above an outlined dirt heap; ghosts fade in from a mist puff while sinking 8 px into place.

effects.name: Level-up ring
effects.how: Ellipse rings (radius 4…40 in steps of 3, y squashed 1.25) in rgb(255,230,170) expand over 0.6 s, with 18 embers and 4 souls.

effects.name: Hurt
effects.how: Red 60 × 50 light on the hero, orange/yellow sparks, and a screen overlay: light base multiplied at hurtT × 0.35 plus #6a0010 at hurtT × 0.18.

ui.summary: Iron-framed bars and boxes (2-px grey frame, 2-px black outline, inset black line, hard drop shadow), pixel numbers in Silkscreen with hard black shadows, blackletter labels in warm #f0a850. Level-up cards look like tarot cards: navy-violet radial background, tarnished gold double border, pixel corner ornaments, arched icon window, Pirata One names and italic IM Fell English descriptions.

motion: Hero: 4 walk frames at the run anim rate, 2 idle frames alternating at 1.6 Hz (bob ±1 px), scarf tail cycles 4 positions.
Small enemies: 4 frames (bob 0/−1, tilt ±1, leaves sway ±7°, alternate root-leg lifts) at anim × 1.6; brutes 4 frames at anim × 2.
Ghosts: 4 frames at 7 fps (tail wave phase, arm reach 0–2 px), hover 4 px plus a ±1.5 px sine at 3 rad/s, drawn at 86% alpha with a 3-pixel icy trail.
Lights flicker continuously (noise + 23 rad/s sine); lanterns cycle 3 eye frames at 10 fps and sway ±1 px.
Gems cycle a glint down the facet in 4 frames at 5 fps (frame 3 held), bob ±1 px; candle flames 3 frames at 9 fps.
Mist layers drift slowly (5 and −7 px/s horizontally); cloud light drifts at (7, 3) px/s.
do: Paint sprites per pixel from lit shapes and quantise into ramps with Bayer-8 dither.
Author colours fully lit and let one multiplied light map create the night.
Give the hero a large warm light and put all warm colour on light sources.
Draw eyes, faces, flames, gems and numbers after the light pass so they glow.
Use banded (posterised + dithered) light falloff, never smooth gradients.
Outline every sprite with #0b0910 and give props a sheared moon shadow toward the lower right.
Break material borders into single tufts, stones and leaves using per-pixel thresholds.
dont: Don't make the world pitch black: ambient moonlight is ~45% brightness blue, and entities only get 55% of the darkening.
Don't use saturated or warm colours on ordinary surfaces.
Don't use smooth radial gradients or blur for lights and fog.
Don't draw emissive details before the light pass (they would be darkened).
Don't use hard material borders or tile repetition on the ground.
Don't add pure #000000 outlines or thick linework.
Don't overlap too many warm lights — the hero must stay the brightest point.
performance: Init is heavy: six 256² tileable ground textures, ~30 gravestones, 4 trees, all character frames, ~20 light sprites, fog and cloud textures are baked once. Ground chunks are generated per pixel in a generator that yields every 16 rows (biome fields on an 8-px grid, bilinear). Per frame: one light-map rebuild (copy + cloud tiles + one drawImage per light), two full-buffer multiplies, a handful of bloom blits, and per-pixel fillRects for eyes/embers. Keep point lights to a few dozen and reuse the light-map canvas.
